From the vector addition and scalar multiplication rules, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}[f(t)+4g(t)]\,\text{d}t={\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t+4{\int }_{1}^{3}g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}[f(t)+4g(t)]\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t+4{\int }_{1}^{3}g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,\sqrt{3}-1,\,2⟩+4⟨\frac{3}{4},\,\frac{1}{2},\,-\frac{5}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,\sqrt{3}-1,\,2⟩+⟨3,\,2,\,-10⟩ \\  & =⟨3+\operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,\sqrt{3}+1,\,-8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
